additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise, or misuse of laxatives to prevent weight gain. Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight, but individuals typically maintain a body weight within or near the normal range, distinguishing it from classic anorexia nervosa. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, interpersonal difficulties, and body-image concerns. It is differentiated from binge-eating disorder by the regular use of compensatory behaviors and from normal overeating by the degree of loss of control and distress associated with the eating episodes.

patient.personality: Lori is a warm, socially engaged planner who channels her anxiety into meticulous organizing of meaningful cultural and community experiences.
patient.stressor: Lori’s current difficulties began after her adult children moved out of state within a short span of time, leaving her and her spouse adjusting to a quieter home and renegotiated roles after decades of parenting and community organizing. With more unstructured time and fewer daily caretaking tasks, she became increasingly preoccupied with how she looked and aged, especially when reconnecting with old acquaintances at arts events or seeing photos of herself alongside younger participants in her intergenerational programs. She began comparing her body harshly to both younger women and to her own image from earlier years, tying her sense of competence and attractiveness as a community leader to how slim and polished she appeared at events. Over several months, this growing focus on weight and shape drove more rigid and then chaotic eating and exercise habits behind the scenes, and when she noticed that her mood and self-worth were swinging dramatically based on the scale and how her clothes fit, she sought psychiatric help at the urging of a close friend from her book club who was worried about how consumed she had become with her appearance.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like how much I weigh and how my body looks has started to completely dictate how I feel about myself, and it’s really wearing me down.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Lately, when I’m getting dressed for a concert or a community event, I’ll stand in front of the mirror and zoom in on every lump and soft spot, and if I think my stomach looks even a little bigger, I feel like a frumpy imposter who has no business being up front organizing anything.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After a bad night where I’ve overeaten, I’ll punish myself by having just coffee and maybe an apple the whole next day and then forcing myself through long power walks and YouTube workout videos even when my knees ache, telling myself I don’t deserve dinner unless I’ve ‘made up for it.’

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: What’s been happening is that I’ll come home after an event, feeling wound up and critical of how I looked in photos, and I’ll start with a piece of leftover quiche or some crackers and cheese, and before I know it I’ve gone through half a loaf of bread, a tub of hummus, cookies, and whatever else is in the pantry, eating standing up in the kitchen long after my husband’s gone to bed.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: In those moments, it feels like a switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in, hearing this tiny voice saying, ‘You need to stop, you’re going to feel awful,’ but my hands keep reaching and chewing like I’m on autopilot and I can’t make myself put it all away until I’m uncomfortably full and ashamed.
